text:
anya: FYI getting a 500 in prod for /v1/generate, dashboard shows request_id=0f4a9c2a. trace UI links to spans but I can't find raw request or the pod logs. where do people usually hunt this down?

sam: start with the Trace view -> open the root span -> click 'Linked request' (if present) which drops you into the Request console.

clara: if the request console doesn't show the body, try searching logs by request header. we use `x-request-id` in gateways. quick stern example:```bash
stern -n prod gateway --since 20m | grep 0f4a9c2a
```

mike: you can also use the console CLI helper (redwoodctl) to pull raw request and pre-roll logs:```bash
redwoodctl requests get --id 0f4a9c2a --raw
redwoodctl logs --request-id 0f4a9c2a --since 30m
```

anya: I don't have redwoodctl locally. any web-only steps?

sam: web path: Console -> Observability -> Requests -> paste request_id -> open timeline -> from there you can jump to any linked span or logs panel. sometimes the Request view is missing body due to retention, then you need pod logs.

clara: if the trace link is only a span id, copy span id, open Traces -> search by span id -> click 'Trace details' -> there should be a "Related requests" card. on older traces that card is empty, then fallback to stern/kubectl.

ops-bot: deploybot: new gateway deploy at 1719876000 — if your request_ts < deploy_ts consider log rotation around that time :rotating_light:

mike: another useful one-liner (GCP Stackdriver / Cloud Logging) if you have access:```bash
gcloud logging read "jsonPayload.request_id=\"0f4a9c2a\"" --limit 50 --project=redwood-prod --format="json"
```

clara: small tip: if you're chasing a trace_id instead of request_id, in console Traces UI you can click the trace and then in the span list look for `x-request-id` or `request.id` attribute. that maps back to request console.

anya: thanks — stern worked. found the 500 stacktrace in gateway and then followed the span to a model-worker pod where the payload is present. saved the raw payload. :thumbsup:

sam: nice. if you paste the span link here I can add it to the incident ticket and tweak the alert to include the `x-request-id` in future notifications.

anya: https://console.redwood.com/traces/trace/abcd1234/span/efgh5678 — added to ticket #INC-4521

mike: one follow-up: we should add a small runbook note under Observability -> Quick hunts: preferred order = Trace -> Request console -> stern -> kubectl logs -> cloud logging. short checklist helps oncall.

clara: +1. I'll add a one-pager with the stern and redwoodctl examples (and note on retention) in the Observability docs.

anya: awesome, thanks all.
